Produce Consolidated Class Lists

Source: R/class_list_functions.R
produce_class_lists.Rd

Produces a consolidated class list by aggregating student and class information and selecting one teacher record per student.

The function supports the package's configurable column-name system, converting input columns to internal names before processing and restoring configured names in the output.

Usage

produce_class_lists(
  data,
  class_name_column = "class_name",
  default_teacher = "Reception teacher",
  default_teacher_FN = "Reception",
  default_teacher_SN = "Teacher"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing student, class and teacher information. Required columns include establishment identifiers, student identifiers, student names, date of birth, UPN, class name and teacher details.

class_name_column

Character string specifying the class-name column to use. Accepts an internal column key or its configured name. Defaults to `"class_name"`.

default_teacher

Character string used when the selected teacher's full name is missing. Defaults to `"Reception teacher"`.

default_teacher_FN

Character string used when the selected teacher's first name is missing. Defaults to `"Reception"`.

default_teacher_SN

Character string used when the selected teacher's surname is missing. Defaults to `"Teacher"`.

Value

A data frame containing one row per unique establishment-student combination, including:

  • Establishment identifiers and school information.

  • Consolidated class names.

  • Student names, date of birth and UPN.

  • Selected teacher's full name, first name and surname.

Column names are returned using the package's configured naming convention.

Details

The function performs the following steps:

  1. Converts input column names to the internal naming convention.

  2. Validates the required columns and selected class-name field.

  3. Groups records by establishment ID and Wonde student ID.

  4. Aggregates student information and all unique class names.

  5. Selects one teacher record per student, prioritising records marked as the main teacher. Where multiple records have equal priority, the first record is selected.

  6. Retains the selected teacher's full name, first name and surname together.

  7. Replaces missing teacher name fields with the specified defaults.

  8. Converts student names to title case and sorts the output.

  9. Restores the configured column names.

Class information is aggregated independently of teacher selection. Students assigned to multiple classes therefore retain all unique class names, even though only one teacher is reported.

Teacher selection is performed within each establishment using the combination of `est_wonde_id` and `s_wonde_id`.

This function is typically used after `clean_class_names()` and `reduce_to_best_teacher()`.

See also

Other class_list: add_student_to_school_class(), clean_teacher_names(), create_school_blanks(), reduce_to_best_teacher(), remove_class(), remove_school_from_class_list(), remove_student_from_class(), update_class_name(), update_class_teacher(), update_school_name(), update_student_class()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
class_list <- produce_class_lists(data)

class_list <- produce_class_lists(
  data,
  class_name_column = "CLASS_WONDE_NAME"
)
} # }
